ambiguity.finding: The Non-Functional Requirements section uses unmeasurable language — 'fast enough that users do not notice any delay' and 'a high volume of link creations during peak traffic without degrading' — where a concrete threshold was needed.

nfrs.finding: The Non-Functional Requirements section makes quantitative performance and capacity claims ('fast enough', 'high volume of link creations during peak traffic') without stating any number or unit.
